LaneX desk lane — wiring card

Terasic DE10-Lite (MAX 10 10M50DAF484C7G) · GPIO header JP1 · pins as in lanex.qsf

Print: A4 landscape. Generated from the same pin table as the FPGA project.
5 V never reaches an FPGA pin.The MAX 10 pins are not 5 V tolerant. Pin 11 (5 V) goes to the ultrasonic VCC only, and its Echo goes through the divider: Echo → 1 kΩ → pin 3, and pin 3 → 2 kΩ → GND.
Measure first.Board on, nothing plugged: multimeter pin 29 → pin 30 = 3.3 V, pin 11 → pin 12 = 5 V. That proves you hold the header the right way round.
Wire with the board unplugged.Then plug the USB in. With nothing wired the board still works: in manual mode (SW8) KEY1 is the vehicle, and the displays run the whole demo.

The gantry

One sensor, 15–25 cm above the table, looking straight down at the lane. At power-up the lane must be empty: the board learns the floor. Push each toy under it at walking pace for a toy: the display shows the height it measured (h  4.5 = 4.5 cm); LEDR1 lights for a lorry (from 6 cm; TALL_MM in lanex.qsf).

Parts

PartQtyNote
Ultrasonic sensor HC-SR04 (4 pins: VCC Trig Echo GND)1Mounted above the lane, looking down: it measures each vehicle's height. VCC from pin 11 (5 V).
Resistors 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ (or 2 × 1 kΩ in series)1 eachThe Echo divider: 5 V → 3.3 V. Never wire Echo straight to the board.
LED + resistor: green, red, yellow (330 Ω) and white (100 Ω)1 eachLong leg (anode) to the resistor, the resistor to the GPIO pin; short leg to GND. A 3-LED traffic-light module (resistors built in) also works.
Buzzer (one of these)1Active, sealed underneath (TMB12A05): + leg to pin 8, − to GND. Passive, green board visible underneath: pin 10 → 330 Ω → buzzer → GND, never without the 330 Ω and never on pin 8. A 3-pin module: VCC 29, GND, I/O pin 8; if it sounds while idle, flip SW6.
USB-UART 3.3 V: Cytron UC00C (CH340), or CP2102 / FT2321Slide its switch to 3.3 V (it sets the signal level too). TXO/TXD → pin 1, RXI/RXD → pin 2, GND → pin 12. VCC, DTR and CTS stay unconnected.
Mini breadboard (170 points) + female-female and male-female jumpers1 + ~20The divider sits here; pin 30 (GND) is the rail for the LEDs, the buzzer and the divider.
Toy car, and a toy lorry clearly taller than the car1 eachThe height difference is the classifier (default: lorry from 6 cm).

Controls

SW0Lane closed (the chip lights P7)
SW2:SW1Class: 00 the sensor's height · 01 van · 10 lorry · 11 motorcycle
SW5:SW3Tag the next vehicle carries
SW6Buzzer module is low-level trigger (pin 8 only)
SW7Mute the buzzer
SW8Manual: KEY1 is the vehicle (no sensor needed)
SW9Tour: replay the 12 AWS tests → PASS12
KEY0Hold: reset (lamp test, banner, Id.56dE); the sensor relearns the floor
KEY1Manual vehicle (SW8 up), else: fingerprint the ROM

Tag presets (SW5:SW3)

  • 0 nonE
  • 1 CAr
  • 2 LorrY
  • 3 CAb
  • 4 StOLEn
  • 5 CLOnE
  • 6 bAd
  • 7 FAr

Lights

LEDR0Something is under the sensor (sensor check)
LEDR1That vehicle is tall: a lorry
LEDR2The chip sees a vehicle (P0)
LEDR3The laptop is sending
LEDR4–7The chip's lamps: charged, camera, alarm, closed
LEDR8The last record was signed
LEDR9Self-check: the ROM fingerprint matches (or PASS12)

Bring-up

  1. Program the .sof: lamp test, banner, Id.56dE, LEDR9.
  2. SW9 up: PASS12. SW9 down.
  3. SW8 up, tag CAr, press KEY1: CHArGE / 2.50.
  4. Wire the sensor + divider (board unplugged); power up with the lane empty; a toy under it: LEDR0.
  5. Wire the lamps and buzzer; push the car, then the lorry.
  6. USB-UART + lanex_live.html in Chrome.
  7. Program the .pof: it boots by itself.
